On May 26, 2026 the Griffin Board of Commissioners voted unanimously to approve amendments to the Unified Development Code (UDC) establishing special-use-permit regulation of data centers in Planned Industrial Districts (PID), confirmed directly by the Griffin Daily News. Minor facilities (up to 10,000 sq ft) and major facilities (10,001-275,000 sq ft) are allowed with setback (1,000/1,500 ft from residences), buffer, noise, Tier 4F generator, decommissioning-bond, and development-agreement conditions; hyperscale/campus data centers are prohibited. This permanent ordinance superseded the Jan. 13, 2026 moratorium ahead of its scheduled July 12, 2026 expiration. No further amendment or repeal located as of 2026-09-23.
- **Outcome:** Permanent UDC amendment adopted May 26, 2026 regulating data centers by special use permit in Planned Industrial Districts; prohibits hyperscale/campus facilities.

- **Normalized date:** `2025-09-16` (unverified)

- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `ga-jones-county-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Jones County M-2 Data Center Ordinance (comprehensive land use plan / land use amendment adding data centers as a conditional use in M-2 industrial zoning), adopted unanimously (5-0) at a called Board of Commissioners meeting on January 16, 2026, replacing the rescinded September 2025 zoning amendments and the intervening October 2025 moratorium.
- **What prompted it:** Legal notice defects under Georgia zoning procedure law and project-pressure concerns
- **Affected projects:** Developer withdrew 600-plus-acre rezoning proposal after public opposition
- **Detailed status:** Replaced, as of 2026-09-23. The January 16, 2026 M-2 Data Center Ordinance (conditional use in M-2 industrial zoning, with 200-foot setbacks, 400-foot setbacks for noise-generating buildings, up to 200-foot buffers, 55/45 dB noise limits, and closed-loop cooling requirements) remains in force but is under active legal challenge: 17 Jones County residents filed a declaratory-judgment lawsuit in February 2026 seeking to void the ordinance on due-process and Georgia Zoning Procedures Law grounds; the county filed a motion to dismiss in March 2026, and as of a Jones County Development Authority meeting reported by The Jones County News, the judge had not yet set a hearing on that motion, with the attorney estimating a 2027 timeline. The litigation has effectively frozen marketing of the underlying Griswoldville Industrial Park site.
- **Outcome:** Reset to re-adopt defensible zoning controls

The Troup County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved the final data center zoning ordinance and lifted the moratorium at a regular meeting, per direct LaGrange Daily News coverage of the vote (County Attorney Mark DeGennaro noted at that meeting that the moratorium was still in force, through June 12, 2026, at the time of the vote). The adopted ordinance restricts all data centers to industrial zoning via special-use permit, requires closed-loop cooling and public water/sewer connection, sets a 1,500-foot setback from sensitive receptors (residences, schools, daycares, hospitals, places of worship, parks, and related site improvements), Tier 4 backup generators, and a 40-foot maximum height. No further change located as of 2026-09-23.
- **Outcome:** UDO review and possible extension
